question: Where can I get a list of desalination plants in the United States, with location, capacity, technology, operator and status?

answer.summary: No current national list of desalination plants was found. Reclamation's 2018 survey (Report 207) counts 406 municipal plants of 0.025 mgd or more and details 58 to 84 of them with owner, technology, start year and design and average production in mgd, but no coordinates, no status and no industrial plants. Texas (TWDB, 60 operating plants in August 2024) and California (2019 maps of 12 existing and 6 proposed seawater facilities) add state views, and operators such as Tampa Bay Water publish plant status. Capacity is stated as design, permitted, average or deliverable depending on the source.
main_caveats: Reclamation's inventory is municipal only and dated December 2018: 406 plants are counted but per-plant files cover 84 (TX, FL, CA built since 2010) and 58 summaries.
Reclamation mixes design, permitted and average capacity and does not flag closed plants; it has no coordinates and no status field.
Capacity is not one measure: Carlsbad shows design 54 mgd and average 50 mgd; Tampa Bay Water states up to 12 mgd at restart and 20 mgd when complete.
Texas's database lists operating public-water-supply plants above 0.025 mgd only; its web application could not be opened because TLS verification failed.
California's seawater maps are from 2019 and also name power-plant, aquarium and oil-facility sites besides municipal plants.
Industrial and brackish plants outside Texas, Florida and California were not covered by any per-plant source found.
answer.confidence_reason: Four official or operator sources read with counts and a Carlsbad cross-check; no current national plant list and several sources unreadable or dated.

attributes.note: Reclamation gives city or county only; California's 2019 maps give map symbols; no coordinates found. Texas viewer not readable.
attributes.gap_note: No coordinates were found in the sources opened. TWDB's web application failed TLS verification and was not read, and Florida's state registers and OpenEI files were not opened.

attributes.note: Design and average production in mgd for 47 and 27 of 58 Reclamation summaries; Texas totals 172 mgd for 60 plants; Tampa Bay Water states 12 to 20 mgd. Measures differ.
attributes.gap_note: Capacities are design, permitted, average or deliverable depending on the source; Reclamation says its totals mix them. Per-plant Texas records, California and other states' registers were not read.

attributes.note: Reclamation summaries name the process for 57 of 58 plants (RO 40, NF 9, MF/RO 3, UF/RO 2, others 3); no per-plant technology for the other plants of the 406.
attributes.gap_note: The 406-plant database is described but only plants built since 2010 are detailed in files found. Texas and California registers were not read for process type.

attributes.note: Reclamation gives the facility owner for 55 of 58 plants; Tampa Bay Water names its operating partner. Owner is not always operator.
attributes.gap_note: No dedicated operator field was found; owners and operators may differ. Other operators and state registers were not checked.

attributes.note: Existing vs proposed only in California's 2019 maps; Reclamation gives a start year but no status; Tampa Bay Water posted an outage and restart in 2024.
attributes.gap_note: Reclamation notes that some older plants have closed without flagging them. Current construction or planned stages were not checked, and the Texas database lists operating plants only.

sources.summary: Reclamation's 2018 survey of U.S. municipal desalination plants, with per-plant owner, technology, start year and design and average production in mgd for the plants it details.
sources.coverage_note: Municipal plants only; 406 plants counted in 35 states, but per-plant files cover 84 (TX, FL, CA built since 2010) and 58 summaries. No coordinates or status.

coverage.geographic: United States, 35 states for the 406 plants counted; Appendix A lists only Texas, Florida and California plants built since 2010; Appendix B has 58 summaries in 15 states

unit.value: One plant per entry. The report counts 406 municipal plants identified from 1971 through 2017 at 0.025 mgd or more; Appendix A (master spreadsheet) holds 84 plants (Texas 53, Florida 19, California 12) and Appendix B holds 58 facility summaries.
unit.quote: The figures are based on 406 municipal desalination plants identified from 1971 through 2017 of size 0.025 mgd or greater.

inclusion_rule.value: Municipal plants only: the survey eliminated pilot or demonstration plants, plants built before 2010 (for the 2018 update), industrial plants and future proposals.
inclusion_rule.quote: Being industrial rather than municipal facilities

reference_date.value: Report dated December 2018; a date cell in the spreadsheet reads 2018-08-31.

exclusions.value: Capacities are mixed: design, permitted and average; older and smaller plants may be closed and are not flagged.
exclusions.quote: Total capacity is approximate, due to some smaller, older plants no longer operating and due to capacities reported in different ways, including design capacity, permitted capacity, and average capacity.

key_fields.meaning: Plant name and owner (not necessarily operator).
Drinking water, water reclamation, aquifer recharge; municipal scope.
Reverse osmosis, nanofiltration, EDR, with pretreatment such as MF/UF.
Design and average desalted production in million gallons per day.

key_fields.field: Start year of RO operation / Source water
key_fields.meaning: Start year (no status field) and source water: seawater, groundwater, surface water, wastewater effluent.

key_fields.field: Appendix A columns COUNTY, CITY, TYPE, PURPOSE, MGD, START, DESAL DESIGN PRODUCTION, DESAL AVERAGE PRODUCTION
key_fields.meaning: Spreadsheet version for Texas, Florida and California plants.

how_to_use.example_request: https://www.usbr.gov/research/dwpr/reportpdfs/report207appendixB.pdf  (entry 'Claude Bud Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant, CA')
how_to_use.example_result: Owner Poseidon Water; purpose drinking water; technology reverse osmosis; start 2015; RO design production 54 mgd; average production 50 mgd; source water seawater from power plant cooling water.
steps: Download report207.pdf for counts and definitions, report207appendixB.pdf for facility summaries and report207appendixA.xlsx for the master spreadsheet.
Read design and average production separately; do not treat them as one capacity.
Cross-check a plant against its operator's page or the state database before using status.
reading_traps: Appendix A contains 84 plants and Appendix B 58, against 406 plants in the report text: the full list is not published in the files found.
No coordinates and no status field: only city or county and a start year; closed plants are not flagged.
Design production is numeric in 47 of 58 summaries and average production in 27; both appear in 24, and are equal in 2.
Industrial plants are excluded, so the inventory is not a full list of U.S. desalination capacity.
Headings use inconsistent state codes (for example 'Fl' and 'FL').

problems: records_total counts plant rows in Appendix A (84); the 406-plant database itself was not found as a file.
report207appendixA.pdf answers 300 (the file is an XLSX); report207appendixC.pdf answers 404.
Counts of design and average production in Appendix B come from text extraction of the PDF.

evidence.quote: Potable water plants (379) far outnumber WWTP plants (24), which outnumber recharge/ASR plants (3).
Municipal desalination plants are now in 35 states (up from 26 in 2002 and 32 in 2009).
not all of the plants included in the total numbers and other statistics are currently in operation

open_questions: Texas plant records. Start: the TWDB desalination web application (TLS verification failed from this environment). Next: open it from a browser or another network and read capacity, source water and location per plant.

Florida: state registers for desalination plants (for example FDEP or water management districts). Start: Reclamation Appendix A lists 19 Florida plants; Tampa Bay Water page. Next: find the state register and compare.
Current status of California facilities and proposals, such as Doheny, after the 2019 maps. Start: State Water Board and project pages. Next: compare with Reclamation and operator pages.
The Mickley database of 406 plants: is it downloadable? Start: OpenEI record files (not downloaded). Next: download the 2018 survey and the CA/FL spreadsheet and compare with Appendices A and B.
Industrial desalination plants (power, mining, oil and gas) and thermal plants. Start: none found. Next: search EIA, state industrial permits and operator reports.

Carlsbad cross-check against its operator and permit: operator sites returned 403 to the command-line client. Next: read the plant's permit or the San Diego County Water Authority page from a browser.

history.note: Read Reclamation Report 207 and both appendices, the TWDB database page and 2024 report, California maps and one operator post. Effort level of the run was not independently known to the model.
